DURATION 15 SECONDS | HORIZONTAL 16:9
CHARACTER REFERENCES
{{CHAR_ZAHHAK}}  {{CHAR_DOCK_WORKERS}}
LOCATION REFERENCES
{{LOC_BALCONY}}  {{LOC_WORKING_QUAY}}
PROP REFERENCES
{{PROP_ZAHHAK_STAFF}}  {{PROP_MOORING_ROPE}}  {{PROP_MERCHANT_BOATS}}
DIRECTION AND CONTINUITY
Create a 15-second horizontal 16:9 live-action cinematic sequence. Preserve each referenced identity, costume, proportions and rigid handmade mask; mask geometry and eye openings remain fixed. All visible humans wear their referenced masks. Emotion comes from posture, hands, breath and visible eyes. Each listed hard cut changes the physical camera station, lens or viewpoint. Handheld movement follows a possible path and recovers focus on essential action. References anchor design; written lighting controls illumination. Tactile modern Iranian mythological design, analog realism and natural imperfections. NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
Zahhak remains unhurried and indifferent. Whenever he walks, show the staff planting first, weight transferring onto it, then the weaker leg following in an uneven step. Preserve the reference's weak-leg side. His two single-headed shoulder snakes remain alive, making small independent movements; preserve their attachment and proportions.
LOCATION AND LIGHT
Cold full night. Balcony rail lights barely define Zahhak's silhouette. The working harbor below is somewhat brighter, with practical loading lamps reflected in water. In quay details, a neutral work lamp reveals wet rope and a fixed bollard. The world remains visually functional.
START STATE AND BLOCKING
Zahhak stands at the north balcony rail facing the harbor, staff planted and weight settled. The industrial saw is behind him inside the residence, entirely outside the frame. A small ordinary merchant vessel is being secured at the quay below.

PLAN 12 | SHOTS
SHOT 12-01 | 0s–7s | 7 SECONDS
18mm wide from behind Zahhak, slightly west of the balcony doorway. He occupies the right third, facing the harbor. Hold nearly still. At roughly two seconds into the shot, the industrial machine starts somewhere behind camera. Zahhak keeps watching the harbor without turning or changing posture. His snakes make small living adjustments. Workers below continue hauling a mooring line.
SHOT 12-02 | 7s–11s | 4 SECONDS
35mm quay-level lateral medium-wide. Two masked dock workers secure an ordinary merchant boat. One feeds the mooring line while the other draws it around a fixed bollard. Water and timber shift under normal docking forces. Their attention stays entirely on work. The off-screen machine sound continues as an editorial sound bridge, quieter beneath quay sounds.
SHOT 12-03 | 11s–15s | 4 SECONDS
65mm close detail beside the bollard. A worker's hands complete the mooring hitch, pulling its final turn snug. Hold the rope visibly taking tension. Immediately after the knot settles, the distant machine sound stops. Allow a brief beat of ordinary water and rope sound, then CUT TO BLACK at the end of the block.
END STATE AND EDIT
The mooring knot holds. The machine has stopped. End immediately after the brief continuation of ordinary harbor sound. Jamshid's death remains entirely off-screen; the final image belongs to work.
SOUND
Ordinary industrial motor and cutting mechanism outside frame, without bodily impact or anatomical sound effects; harbor water, timber movement and rope friction. At the final knot, machine stops, ordinary water persists briefly, then black and silence.
NO MUSIC. NO DIALOGUE.
